chunks: Al-Tawhid: Al-Hamdani, from Ali, from his father, from Al-Harawi who said: I said to Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him): O son of the Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the report narrated by the Ahl al-Hadith that 'the believers will visit their Lord from their homes in Paradise'?

He (peace be upon him) said: O Abu Salt, indeed Allah Blessed and Exalted favored His prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) over all His creation from the prophets and the angels. He made obedience to him obedience to Him, and pledging allegiance to him pledging allegiance to Him, and visiting him in this world and the hereafter visiting Him. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah' and He said: 'Those who pledge allegiance to you are in fact pledging allegiance to Allah, the hand of Allah is over their hands.' And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever visits me in my lifetime or after my death has visited Allah.' The station of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) in Paradise is the highest of stations, so whoever visits him to his station in Paradise from his home has visited Allah Blessed and Exalted.

He said: I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, what is the meaning of the report they narrate that 'the reward of 'La ilaha illa Allah' is looking at the Face of Allah'? He (peace be upon him) said: O Abu Salt, whoever describes Allah with a face like the faces (of humans) has disbelieved. But the Face of Allah is His prophets, His messengers, and His proofs, may the prayers of Allah be upon them. They are the ones through whom one turns towards Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and towards His religion and knowledge of Him. And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Everyone upon it will perish, and will remain the Face of your Lord' and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Every thing is perishing except His Face.' Thus, looking at the prophets of Allah, His messengers, and His proofs (peace be upon them) in their stations is a great reward for the believers on the Day of Judgment.

And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever hates my Ahl al-Bayt and my progeny will not see me, nor will I see him on the Day of Judgment.' And he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Among you is one who will not see me after he separates from me.' O Abu Salt, indeed Allah Blessed and Exalted is not described by space, nor is He perceived by sight and imagination.

He said: I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, inform me about Paradise and the Fire, are they created today? He said: Yes, and indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered Paradise and saw the Fire when he was ascended to the heavens. He said: I said to him: There is a group that says 'they are destined today but not yet created.' He (peace be upon him) said: Those are not from us, nor are we from them. Whoever denies the creation of Paradise and the Fire has lied against the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and lied against us, and is not from our Wilayah in any way, and will abide forever in the Fire of Hell. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'This is Hell which the criminals deny. They will go around between it and scalding water.'

And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When I was ascended to the heavens, Jibril took my hand and brought me into Paradise. He handed me some of its fresh dates, and I ate them, and that became seed in my loin. When I descended to the earth, I met Khadija, and she became pregnant with Fatima. Fatima is a human Houri. Whenever I longed for the scent of Paradise, I smelled the scent of my daughter Fatima.'

key_terms.الْأَهْلُ وَالْعِتْرَة: The Family and Progeny (of the Prophet)
key_terms.وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah (interpreted as the Imams/Prophets)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning of 'visiting Allah' and 'looking at His Face' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Ali al-Rida (AS) elucidates the Shia doctrine of *Ziyarat* by equating the Prophet and Imams as the ultimate manifestations of Divine attributes, where obedience to them constitutes obedience to Allah. He clarifies that 'visiting God' and 'beholding His Face' are metaphorical for recognizing the *Hujjah* (Divine Proof) in the Hereafter, distinguishing this from the physical vision of God, who is beyond space and imagination. Furthermore, he affirms the pre-existence of Paradise and Hell, citing the Mi'raj as evidence, and links the sensory experience of Paradise to the spiritual presence of Fatimah al-Zahra (SA).
